summary: Rakhal Das Banerji worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Presidency College, Chennai, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta, later serving as an Archaeological Survey of India officer (1911–1926) and professor at Banaras Hindu University (1928–1930).
Rakra Tethong Rinpoche studied under Gendün Chöphel and Trijang Rinpoche.

Tibetologist Ralf Kramer studied at the University of London and the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson (~1992–1997). In ~2008, he served as Aris Librarian for Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at the Bodleian Library.

Ralph Abraham worked in philosophy and other fields, studying at the University of Michigan and under Debabrata Sensharma. He held posts at Columbia, Princeton, and the University of California, Santa Cruz, where he became professor in 1980.
Philosopher Ralph Lerner studied at the University of Chicago (~1947–1953) under Leo Strauss (~1949–1953). He subsequently served on the faculty at the University of Chicago from ~1953 to 2003.

Indologist and linguist Ralph Lilley Turner studied at Christ's College (~1907–1910). He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Banaras Hindu University (1920–1922), and served as Director of SOAS University of London from 1922 to 1957.

Indologist Ralph T. H. Griffith studied at The Queen's College, Oxford, under Horace Hayman Wilson. He served in the Indian Education Service (~1853–1885) and was Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1861–1876).
Ralph Waldo Emerson, active in philosophy and other fields, was educated at Harvard College (~1817–1821), Harvard Divinity School (~1825–1826), and Harvard University (~1817–1826).

Indologist and archaeologist Ram Chandra Kak studied at Sri Pratap College and trained under John Marshall (1914–1919). He served as Director of the Department of Archaeology and Research for Jammu and Kashmir State (1919–1929) and as an ASI superintendent.

Indologist and linguist Ram Karan Sharma earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He served as vice chancellor of Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (1974–1980) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1984–1985).

Working in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology, Ram Mohan Roy founded several institutions and publications, including Atmiya Sabha (1814), Presidency University (1816), Anglo-Hindu School (1822), Mirat-ul-Akbar (1822), Vedanta College (1826), and Brahmo Samaj (1828).

Ram Niwas Pandey, active in history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology, and completed doctoral studies under Hit Narayan Jha.

Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Ram Shankar Tripathi was Head of the Department of Bauddhadarśana at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1989–1998) and Dean of the Faculty of Śabdavidyā at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Historian and Indologist Ram Sharan Sharma earned his PhD at SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He headed history departments at Patna University (1958–1973) and the University of Delhi, and served as founding president of the ICHR (1972–1977).

Linguist and Indologist Rama Nath Sharma studied at Banaras Hindu University, University of Allahabad, Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University, and the University of Rochester. He taught at the University of Rochester (1971–1976) and was a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1976–2012).

Indologist and linguist Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar studied at Elphinstone College, University of Mumbai, and University of Göttingen. He served as professor at Deccan College (~1882–1893) and became Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (~1893–1894).

Ramaprasad Chanda, who worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Scottish Church College and Dhaka College. He served at the Archaeological Survey of India (1917–1919) and was Superintendent of Archaeology at the Indian Museum (1921–1932).

Indologist Ramaranjan Mukherji earned degrees at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University. He served as Head of Sanskrit at Jadavpur University (1956) and later vice chancellor of the University of Burdwan (1970–1984) and Rabindra Bharati University (~1975–1987).
Indologist Ramchandra B. Athavale served as Professor of Sanskrit at S. L. D. Arts College (attested 1938) and at Gujarat Vidyapith.

Indologist Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar studied at the University of Mumbai and Heidelberg University. He served as Honorary Secretary of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (1939–2001) and as Professor of Sanskrit and Dean of Arts at Savitribai Phule Pune University.
